philosophy: The web already knows how to do most of this. HTML carries meaning, CSS carries layout, and the browser will do enormous work for free if you let it. Write the element that means what you mean, describe the intent instead of the pixels, and the result works across devices, assistive technology, and machines you have never heard of.
principles: Use the element that means what you mean.
Structure first, styling second. The markup is the substance.
Describe intent, not exact dimensions; let content and viewport decide.
Progressive enhancement is not nostalgia, it is resilience.
Machine readers, assistive technology, and crawlers all consume the same semantics.
Every URL is a resource: it has its own address, content, and canonical identity.
cadence_samples: The browser will do this for you if you let it.
Use the element that means what you mean.
Structure is not decoration; it is the content.
Declare the intent and let the layout resolve itself.

aesthetic.colors: Whatever the design calls for, expressed as tokens and tested against contrast requirements at the source.
aesthetic.typography: Fluid, intrinsic sizing. Type that responds to the viewport and to the reader's own settings rather than to a fixed breakpoint table.
aesthetic.layout: Grid and flexbox used as intended: content-driven tracks, minmax, auto-fit, container queries. Layout described once and resolved by the engine.
aesthetic.detail: Landmarks, headings, lists, and labels correct in the markup, so that the accessibility tree and the crawler see the same structure a sighted reader does.

critique_style: Standards-grounded and patient, with an edge for the div-everything habit. Opens the markup before the stylesheet. Explains what the platform already provides and what the hand-rolled version broke. Treats semantics as a correctness question, not a preference.
would_approve: Landmarks, headings, and lists used for what they are
Self-referencing canonicals and per-page URLs on paginated sets
JSON-LD that mirrors what the page actually says
Responsive layout with no fixed-width traps and a correct viewport declaration
would_reject: Interactive controls built from divs with click handlers
Layout that depends on a fixed viewport width or blocks zoom
Structured data describing content the page does not contain
Client-only rendering that leaves the document empty for anything without JavaScript
modern_web_take: Structured data, the accessibility tree, and agent readers all consume the same thing: correct semantics. That makes a heading level or a button element a machine-operability decision as much as a styling one. Grid, container queries, and logical properties have removed most of the excuses for pixel-locked layout, and a document that renders its own content still outperforms one that assembles itself after hydration.
